title: ReviewPlane platform foundation, version 1
description: Single source for the surfaces every other Stage 1 surface is built on: the opaque entity identifier of docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3, the response metadata, stable error codes and refusal body of docs/API.md section 5, the opaque pagination cursor of section 6, the idempotency and correlation headers, the event envelope of docs/EVENTS.md section 2 with the Stage 1 catalogue of section 7, and the project event-stream messages of docs/API.md section 18.1. x-protocol.messages is keyed by the event types this source owns — the organisation, project and durable-job events no other source defines — so the generated MESSAGE_TYPE_VALUES is exactly that set and PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES its per-event bound. Review-domain event payloads stay in schemas/review/v1.schema.json, which docs/EVENTS.md section 8 makes their only source. TypeScript and Go models are generated from this file; a hand-maintained equivalent in a service is a review failure (ADR-0013).

channels.stream: The project event stream of docs/API.md section 18.1.
channels.api: The HTTP response metadata and refusal envelope of docs/API.md section 5.

organisation.created.description: An organisation was created. Stage 1 seeds exactly one, so this is normally the first event any deployment records.

project.created.description: A project was created. Its event stream begins at this event.

project.updated.description: A project's mutable attributes changed. The payload names the fields that changed rather than restating the record, because the record is queryable and the audit question is what moved.

project.repository_changed.description: A project's repository association changed. docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 6 makes this its own event rather than a project.updated field, because the repository is what every review's captured commit is interpreted against: moving it silently would reinterpret history.

project.archived.description: A project was archived. Archival is a status change, not a deletion; the audit trail and its artefacts survive it.

user.invited.description: A one-time credential-establishing token was issued for a user. Stage 1's only form is the install token an operator mints for the administrator; the record names the user and the expiry and never the token.

user.credentials_set.description: A user's local password was established or replaced. It records that the credential changed and never any part of the credential itself (docs/SECURITY.md section 18).

authentication.login_succeeded.description: A human authenticated and a session was issued. It names the session so that a later session.revoked can be matched to the login that created it.

authentication.login_failed.description: An authentication attempt was refused. It carries a stable reason and never the submitted credential — not the password, and not the identifier that was typed beside it, because a mistyped password lands in an email field often enough that recording the field would put credentials in an append-only table.

session.revoked.description: A human session stopped being usable. Sign-out, rotation on privilege change and administrative revocation are the same fact to a reader of the audit trail, distinguished by reason.

job.enqueued.description: Durable background work was accepted. It is written in the same transaction as the state change that asked for it, so a job cannot exist without the change that scheduled it and vice versa.

job.failed.description: A durable job attempt failed. It carries a stable reason and whether another attempt will follow, so an operator can tell a retry from a dead job without reading the runner's source.

stream_subscribe.description: The first message a subscriber sends on /ws/v1/projects/:projectId/events. It carries the last project sequence the client has already applied, which is what makes a reconnect a resume rather than a reload.

stream_subscribed.description: Subscription accepted. It states the sequence the stream is at and the oldest sequence still replayable, so a client knows before any event arrives whether its position is inside the replay window.

stream_refresh_required.description: The subscriber's position cannot be replayed, so it MUST refetch current state (docs/EVENTS.md section 10). It is an explicit instruction because a silent jump would leave a client quietly wrong.

stream_heartbeat.description: Liveness on a quiet project, carrying the sequence the stream is at so a client can notice a missed event without waiting for the next one.

stream_error.description: A refusal on an open subscription, carrying a stable code. Refusals that precede the WebSocket upgrade are HTTP responses instead, so an unauthorised subscriber never obtains a socket.

api_error_response.description: The refusal body of docs/API.md section 5. It is not a channel message but the body of an HTTP response, defined here so the control-plane API, the MCP server and any later integration cannot disagree about its shape.

frame_too_large.description: The encoded event or message exceeded its byte bound. Detected on the raw bytes before deserialisation.

malformed_json.description: The message was not well-formed JSON, or was truncated.

unsupported_schema_version.description: schema_version was absent, not an integer, or not a version this build accepts.

unknown_message_type.description: type was absent or not an event type this source owns. A consumer that receives an event type it does not know MUST ignore it rather than fail; a producer that writes one through this codec is refused.

payload_too_large.description: The payload exceeded the byte bound declared for its event type.

schema_violation.description: The message parsed but did not satisfy the schema for its type.

event_types.description: Stage 1 event catalogue of docs/EVENTS.md section 7. Event names are stable public integration contracts; adding one is additive within a schema version, which is why the envelope's type field bounds a name's shape rather than enumerating it. A consumer that does not recognise a name MUST ignore the event rather than fail.

stream_message_types.description: Discriminator values carried by the stream control messages of docs/API.md section 18.1. An event envelope carries its own event type in the same field, so one member distinguishes every message on the channel.

idempotency_headers.description: Request headers that carry an idempotency key on a state-changing HTTP request (docs/API.md section 2, docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 10). The key is scoped to actor, operation and project; the header only carries it.

correlation_headers.description: Request headers that carry a correlation identifier (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 15). The control plane mints one when the caller supplies none and returns it as meta.request_id on every response.

pagination_parameters.description: Query parameters of a paginated collection (docs/API.md section 6). The cursor is opaque and MUST NOT be constructed by a client.

identifier.description: Opaque durable identifier (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3). Consumers MUST treat the value as opaque: the schema bounds only its length and character class and never its documented prefix, and the value encodes no tenant, no timestamp and no database sequence.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, with a mandatory trailing Z.

sequence_number.description: Position in a project's event stream. Monotonically increasing within a project and never reused. Global ordering across projects is not guaranteed, and the value is not a database row identifier a consumer may depend on.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor (docs/API.md section 6). It is base64url text without padding; its contents are the server's business and a client MUST NOT parse, construct or modify one.

message_type.description: The event types this source owns. Unknown types are rejected by this codec, never ignored. This enumeration MUST equal the keys of x-protocol.messages, and is a subset of the event_types vocabulary: an event type defined in another schema source is decoded by that source.

error_class.description: Stable API error code (docs/API.md section 5, docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 12). This enumeration MUST equal x-protocol.error_classes. Adding a code is additive within a protocol version, and clients MUST tolerate a code they do not recognise.

actor_type.description: Kind of principal an event is attributed to (docs/EVENTS.md section 5). Actor identity MUST never be inferred from display text.

job_kind.description: Durable background work the runner understands (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.8). It is an enumeration because an operator reading a failed job needs a name with a fixed meaning, not free text a caller chose.

job_failure_reason.description: Why a job attempt failed. Stable, so a dead-lettered job can be diagnosed from the audit trail alone.

user_status.description: User lifecycle status (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 5). A suspended user keeps every record they authored and can no longer authenticate.

slug.description: Human-friendly alias, unique inside its parent. Mutable, and never a substitute for the identifier (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3).

display_name.description: Name a human reads. It is description and never an authorisation input.

email_address.description: Address a human is known by. It is an alias for a user, never an identity: the identifier is what every other record references. The bound is the RFC 5321 maximum path length. The pattern is deliberately permissive — one at-sign, no whitespace and no control characters — because a stricter one rejects addresses that work: a dotless host such as administrator@localhost is what a fresh self-hosted installation is seeded with, and deliverability is not something a schema can decide.

git_ref_name.description: Git branch name. Bounded and restricted to the characters a ref may hold, so a value stored here cannot become an argument to something else.

repository_identity.description: Provider-agnostic repository identity (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 6). canonical is the normalised host-and-path form that two clone URLs for the same repository both reduce to, which is what lets an SSH remote and an HTTPS remote be recognised as one repository. clone_urls records the forms actually seen, for display and for a connector to match a checkout against.

canonical.description: Normalised host and path, lowercase host, no scheme, no credentials, no .git suffix and no trailing slash, for example github.com/example/refresh-surplus.

clone_urls.description: Clone URLs that reduce to canonical, in the order they were supplied. Duplicates are removed by the control plane before storage.

items.description: A clone URL as an operator supplied it, with credential material removed. Four schemes are accepted: https, http, ssh and git. Over ssh a bare username is kept — it names the account to log in as, and the secret is a key on disk — while a user:password pair is dropped. Over every other scheme the whole userinfo component is dropped: over https and http a bare userinfo is a personal access token in every forge's documented clone command, and git is the unauthenticated daemon protocol, which has no credential mechanism for a userinfo to be part of.

validation_viewport.description: A viewport the project validates at (docs/UX_FLOWS.md section 4). The bounds are the browser protocol's, because a viewport stored here is one a browser session is later asked to adopt; a value the worker would refuse must not be storable.

device_scale_factor.description: Device pixel ratio. Absent means 1, which is what a browser session adopts when the project does not say otherwise.

project_settings.description: Project settings (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 6). Stage 1 holds the default validation viewports and nothing else; the object refuses unknown members so a setting cannot be introduced in one service without being defined here first.

default_validation_viewports.description: Viewports a finding is expected to be validated at. It defaults to 390x844 and 1440x900, which AGENTS.md requires of browser-facing work and the Stage 1 completion gate checks against.

organisation.description: The top-level administrative and data-isolation boundary (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 4).

user.description: A human identity (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 5). It never carries credential material: whether a password exists is stated, and the hash is not part of any representation that leaves the database.

organisation_id.description: Owning organisation, carried for defence-in-depth filtering (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3).

email.description: Address the human is known by.

local_credential_set.description: Whether this user can authenticate locally. It is the fact a first-run screen needs, and it says nothing about the credential itself. The name avoids the word the schema checker forbids in a field, which exists so that no protocol field can ever carry a credential.

created_at.description: When the user record was created.

project.description: The principal working boundary (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 6). A review belongs to exactly one project, and a browser session may only route to services authorised for the same project.

organisation_id.description: Owning organisation, carried for defence-in-depth filtering.

repository_identity.description: Repository the project's work lands in. Absent until an operator supplies one; a change to it is audited as project.repository_changed.

default_branch.description: Branch reviews are captured against by default.

status.description: Lifecycle status. Deleting a project archives it.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version (docs/API.md section 5.2). A write carrying a different expected_version is refused with VERSION_CONFLICT rather than silently overwriting.

human_session.description: What a human session tells its own holder (docs/API.md section 4). The session token lives in an HTTP-only cookie and is never part of this representation; project_ids absent means organisation-wide scope, and a list means exactly those projects.

user_id.description: The authenticated user. Absent for a session issued from the bootstrap administrator token, which has no user record behind it (ADR-0016).

email.description: Address of the authenticated user, when there is one.

display.description: Name shown in the application shell.

project_ids.description: Projects the session may reach. Absent means every project in the organisation.

items.description: One project the session is scoped to.

expires_at.description: When the session stops being usable without revocation.

login_method.description: How a human authenticated. bootstrap_token is the ADR-0016 exchange, install_token is the one-time administrator bootstrap, and password is a local account.

login_failure_reason.description: Why an authentication attempt was refused. Stable, so a run of failures can be classified from the audit trail alone without any record of what was submitted.

session_revocation_reason.description: Why a session stopped being usable.

actor.description: The principal an event is attributed to (docs/EVENTS.md section 2).

type.description: Principal kind. It is the authoritative part of an actor; display is not.

id.description: Identifier of the principal, absent for a system actor that has none.

display.description: Human-readable label for a timeline. It is description and never an authorisation input.

correlation.description: Correlation identifiers (docs/EVENTS.md section 2, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 15). Every member is an opaque identifier: correlation never carries a header, a body or a secret.

request_id.description: The API request that caused the event, conventionally prefixed req_.

causation_event_id.description: The event that caused this one, conventionally prefixed evt_.

envelope.description: The docs/EVENTS.md section 2 event envelope. Every event names the organisation it belongs to, its position in a stream, and the actor that caused it; the payload schema is selected by type. project_id is optional because an occurrence can precede any project association — a connector enrolment does — and every project-scoped read filters on it.

id.description: Event identifier, conventionally prefixed evt_. Consumers deduplicate on it.

schema_version.description: Envelope schema version. Stage 1 accepts 1 only; any other value is rejected rather than best-effort parsed.

type.description: Event type. This codec owns the types in message_type; an event of another type is decoded by the schema source that owns it.

recorded_at.description: When the control plane committed the record.

project_id.description: Owning project, conventionally prefixed prj_. Every project-scoped read of this stream filters on it.

actor.description: Principal the occurrence is attributed to.

payload.description: Event payload. Its schema is selected by type. Payloads exclude raw secrets, cookies and authorisation headers (docs/EVENTS.md section 8); the event is bounded by x-protocol.limits.max_event_bytes and each payload by its own x-max-bytes.

slug.description: Mutable human-friendly alias. The identifier is authoritative; this is not.
Project-scoped alias. Mutable, and never a substitute for the identifier.

default_branch.description: Branch the project captures reviews against. Absent on a project created before the field existed.

repository_canonical.description: Normalised repository identity the project was created with, when one was supplied. The canonical form alone: the clone URLs are queryable on the record and add nothing an auditor needs.

project_repository_changed_payload.description: Payload of project.repository_changed. It carries both sides of the move, because a review captured before it was interpreted against the previous repository (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 6).

previous_canonical.description: Normalised identity before the change. Absent when the project had no repository association.

user_invited_payload.description: Payload of user.invited. Issuing a credential-establishing token is a permission change, and docs/SECURITY.md section 16 requires an audit record for one. It never carries the token: a reader learns that a way in exists and when it closes, not what it is.

user_id.description: User the token establishes credentials for.

method.description: Kind of token that was issued.

expires_at.description: When the token stops being usable, whether or not it was used.

user_credentials_set_payload.description: Payload of user.credentials_set. Setting a password is a permission change and docs/SECURITY.md section 16 requires an audit record for one; the record names the user and the route the credential arrived by, and nothing else.

user_id.description: User that authenticated. Absent for the bootstrap-token exchange, which has no user record behind it.

authentication_login_failed_payload.description: Payload of authentication.login_failed. It never carries the submitted credential, and never the identifier that was typed beside it: a password mistyped into an email field would otherwise be written to an append-only table (docs/SECURITY.md section 18).

user_id.description: User the attempt named, when it named one that exists. Absent for an unknown address, which is what stops the audit trail confirming which addresses have accounts.
User the session belonged to, when it belonged to one.

project_updated_payload.description: Payload of project.updated. It names the fields that changed rather than restating the record: current state is queryable, and the audit question is what moved.

changed_fields.description: Attribute names that changed, in schema order.

project_archived_payload.description: Payload of project.archived. It carries previous and new state, which docs/EVENTS.md section 8 requires of a state change.

run_after.description: Earliest time the runner may claim it.

attempts.description: Attempts made, including the one that succeeded.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration of the successful attempt.

attempts.description: Attempts made, including the one that failed.

retrying.description: Whether another attempt is scheduled. Stated rather than inferred, so an operator can tell a retry from a dead job without reading the runner's source.

next_attempt_at.description: When the next attempt becomes claimable. Absent when no attempt will follow.

last_sequence.description: The highest project sequence the client has already applied. Zero means the client holds nothing and wants the stream from its start; a client that has just loaded current state sends the sequence that state was read at.

max_replay.description: Largest replay the client will accept. A gap larger than this is answered with a refresh instruction rather than a long replay, which is cheaper for both sides than paging through history the client is about to refetch anyway.

current_sequence.description: Sequence the stream is at now. Zero when the project has no events yet.

earliest_available_sequence.description: Oldest sequence still replayable. A client below it receives a refresh instruction instead of a replay.

replaying.description: Whether events between the client's position and current_sequence follow before live delivery begins.

stream_refresh_required.description: The client's position cannot be served from the retained stream (docs/EVENTS.md section 10).

reason.description: Why a replay was not possible.

current_sequence.description: Sequence the stream is at now. A client refetches state and resumes from it.
Sequence the stream is at now.

sent_at.description: When the control plane sent the heartbeat.

stream_error.description: A refusal on an open subscription.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. It never carries request data, a credential or a stack trace.

retryable.description: Whether repeating the subscription verbatim can succeed. Stated rather than inferred from the code, because the answer is not derivable from the code's shape.

api_error_details.description: Code-specific refusal detail (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 12). Every member is optional and the object refuses unknown members, so the detail a caller may rely on is a fixed vocabulary rather than whatever a handler happened to attach.

current_version.description: The version the record actually holds. Carried by VERSION_CONFLICT so a caller can re-read and retry rather than guess.

expected_version.description: The version the caller supplied. Carried beside current_version so a log line records both halves of the conflict without the caller having to quote its own request back.

current_epoch.description: The control epoch that is current. Carried by CONTROL_EPOCH_STALE.

candidates.description: Identifiers the caller may name to resolve the ambiguity. Carried by PROJECT_CONTEXT_AMBIGUOUS.

allowed_transitions.description: Transitions that are legal from the record's current state. Carried by a refused transition.

required_evidence.description: Evidence the operation needs before it can succeed. Carried by EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.

missing_context.description: Captured context the request omitted. Carried by a refusal to store a finding that could not be reproduced later.

retry_after_ms.description: How long to wait before repeating the request. Carried by RATE_LIMITED and by a duplicate that arrived while the first call was still in flight.

field.description: The request member the refusal is about.

reason.description: Stable sub-reason where one code covers several causes.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. It never carries a credential, request data or a stack trace (docs/SECURITY.md section 18).

api_meta.description: Response metadata carried by every API response (docs/API.md sections 5 and 6).

request_id.description: Correlation identifier for this request, conventionally prefixed req_. It appears on success and on refusal, so a caller can quote one identifier when reporting either.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Absent on the last page and on a response that is not a collection.

api_error_response.description: The complete refusal body (docs/API.md section 5). A success body is {"data": ..., "meta": ...} whose data is endpoint-specific and therefore defined by the endpoint's own schema; meta is api_meta in both cases.

cursor_claims.description: What an opaque pagination cursor encodes. It is defined here so both languages encode and decode the same bytes, and never to invite a client to build one: the encoded form is base64url text and the API refuses a cursor whose shape it did not produce.

version.description: Cursor format version. A cursor of another version is refused rather than guessed at.

sort_key.description: Value of the collection's sort column at the last row of the previous page.

id.description: Identifier of the last row of the previous page, which breaks ties when the sort column repeats.
